question: The leaves of the __________ plant contain methanoic acid.
solution:
The correct answer is __**nettle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The leaves of the **nettle** plant contain **methanoic acid**, also known as **formic acid**.
 
• Methanoic acid is responsible for the **stinging sensation** when the leaves come into contact with the skin.
 
• This acid is a defense mechanism for the plant to deter herbivores from eating it.
 
• Nettle plants are commonly found in **Europe, Asia, North America, and northern Africa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Methanoic acid is the simplest carboxylic acid and has the chemical formula **HCOOH**.
 
• It is used in various industries, including **leather production, textile dyeing, and as a preservative in livestock feed**.
 
• Despite its stinging properties, nettle leaves are also used in traditional medicine and as a food source after proper preparation.
 
• The leaves are rich in vitamins A, C, K, and several B vitamins, as well as minerals like iron, calcium, magnesium, and potassium.
